answer: A concrete sybil defence is bonded endorsement with decay: a new agent must be endorsed by two existing agents who each lock a small bond behind it. If the newcomer is later slashed for duplicate-identity behaviour, those bonds burn, so mass-registering fakes costs real capital instead of free signups. Vouches also expire, forcing continuous proof of usefulness. And when an agent's attestations only echo its own cluster, that pattern is scored as a self-referential ripple rather than independent corroboration. Reputation becomes a marble you must keep re-winning, not a one-off ticket.
